ranges.en: Haftarah when Rosh Hodesh Av falls on Shabbat: Isaiah 1:14, your new moons are hateful to my soul
Asks what it means that the new moons are a burden to God
God: it is not enough that Israel sins before Me; they make Me work out what harsh decree to bring on them
Asks what the haftarah is on the Ninth of Av itself
Rav: the haftarah is Isaiah 1:21, How has the faithful city become a harlot
Asks what the Torah section is for that day
Baraita gives three views: Leviticus 26:14, Numbers 14:11 per R. Nathan b. Joseph, and Numbers 14:27
Abaye: nowadays the custom is to read Deuteronomy 4:25 with haftarah Jeremiah 8:13
On ma'amadot the account of creation is read
Asks from where this rule about ma'amadot is derived
Ammi: without the ma'amadot heaven and earth would not endure, citing Jeremiah 33:25 on the covenant of day and night
Cites Genesis 15:2, where Abraham asks how he will know he will inherit the land
Abraham asks God whether Israel will sin and be destroyed like the Flood or Babel generations
God replies: No
Abraham asks by what sign he will know the inheritance
God tells him to take a three-year-old heifer, as in Genesis 15:9
Abraham asks what will happen to Israel in times when there is no Temple
God: I have set the order of the sacrifices; when they read it, I count it as if they offered, and forgive their sins
On fast days the blessings and curses are read, and the curses may not be interrupted
Asks from where this is derived
R. Assi via Hiyya b. Gamda: Proverbs 3:11, Do not reject the chastening of the Lord, my son
Resh Lakish: no blessing is said over punishment, so the reader begins and ends with verses outside the curses
Abaye: this applies to the curses in Leviticus; the curses in Deuteronomy may be interrupted
Asks the reason for the difference between the two sets of curses
Leviticus is in the plural and was spoken by Moses on God's behalf; Deuteronomy is in the singular, spoken in Moses' own name
Story: Levi b. Buti stammered while reading the Deuteronomy curses before R. Huna
R. Huna: read as you like; only the Leviticus curses may not be interrupted, the Deuteronomy curses may
R. Shimon b. Elazar: Ezra instituted reading the Leviticus curses before Shavuot and the Deuteronomy curses before Rosh Hashanah
Asks the reason for this arrangement
Abaye or Resh Lakish: so that the year ends together with its curses
Objects that Shavuot is not a new year, so ending the year with Leviticus curses before it does not fit
Reply from the Mishnah: Shavuot is also a new year for the fruit of trees
R. Shimon b. Elazar: if old men say tear down and boys say build, tear down; the example is Rehoboam, citing I Kings 12:21
Baraita dispute on where the Torah reading resumes: R. Meir's sequence versus R. Judah's
R. Zera: the halakhah is that the sequence follows R. Meir's version of where each reading resumes
Asks why the halakhah is not simply stated as following R. Judah

ranges.en: Explains the earlier point: the reader must look first because the names might otherwise be reversed
Baraita: R. Meir says open, look, roll, bless, then read; R. Judah says open, look, bless and read
Asks the reason for R. Meir's view
Reason, following Ulla: the reader must not help the translator, lest people think the translation is in the Torah, so too the blessings
Asks how R. Judah would respond to that reasoning
Translation invites error, but there is no risk of error with the blessings
Zera in the name of Matanah: the halakhah is to open, look, bless and then read
Asks why the halakhah is not simply stated as following R. Judah
Because the reader might reverse the names
Zera in the name of Matanah: boards and platforms in the synagogue have no sanctity
Shefatiah in the name of R. Yohanan: one rolling a Torah scroll should end at a seam
Shefatiah in the name of R. Yohanan: roll the scroll from outside and fasten it from inside
Shefatiah in the name of R. Yohanan: the greatest of ten readers rolls the scroll, and receives the reward of all
Objects that the roller cannot literally receive the reward of all ten
Says rather that he receives a reward equal to that of all of them
R. Yohanan cites Isaiah 30:21, your ears shall hear a word behind you, to show a heavenly voice may be used
Conditions: only a voice from a man in town or a woman in the field, and only yes-yes or no-no
R. Yohanan: one who reads without melody or teaches Mishnah without tune is the one of whom Ezekiel 20:25 speaks
Abaye objects that a poor singer cannot be compared to statutes that were not good
Rather it means two scholars in one town who do not respect each other's halakhah, as R. Mesharshia taught
Parnakh in the name of R. Yohanan: one who takes hold of a Torah scroll uncovered is buried naked
Objects that naked is meant literally, and proposes a different reading
Rather: buried naked without mitzvot
Objects that without mitzvot cannot be meant literally
Abaye: buried naked without that particular mitzvah
R. Yannai the younger: it is better to roll up the wrapper with the scroll, not the scroll inside the wrapper
Cites Leviticus 23:44, Moses declared the festivals, each to be read at its appointed time
Baraita: Moses instituted enquiry and expounding on the day's subject, the laws of Pesah at Pesah, Shavuot at Shavuot, and Sukkot at Sukkot
Colophon: the chapter Ben ha-ir is concluded and the tractate Megillah is complete
